provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Keeping my body clean
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list two body cleaning methods.
The pupils should be able to state the importance of washing teeth.

Introduction:
We have learned about our body parts. Today we learn how to keep them clean.
Clean body helps us stay healthy and strong.

Content:
Bathing is washing our whole body with soap and water.
We bathe every morning before school.
Washing teeth keeps our mouth clean.
We use toothbrush and toothpaste to wash teeth.

Class activity:
Let us pretend to brush our teeth together.
Show me how you wash your face.

Evaluation questions:
What do we use to wash our teeth?
How often should we bathe?
Why is keeping clean important?

Summary:
Clean body is healthy body.
We wash every day to stay strong.

topics.title: Healthy food
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name three fruits.
The pupils should be able to list two vegetables.

Introduction:
We have learned about our body parts. Today we learn about good food.
Good food helps us grow strong and healthy.

Content:
Fruits are sweet foods from plants.
Examples are banana, orange and mango.
Vegetables are good foods from plants.
Examples are carrot and spinach.
Good foods make us strong.

Class activity:
Let us name all the fruits we know.
Each pupil will say one vegetable.

Evaluation questions:
Name one fruit you like.
What vegetable did you eat yesterday?
Why should we eat good food?

Summary:
Fruits and vegetables are good food.
They help us grow strong and healthy.

topics.title: Safety at home
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify two sharp objects.
The pupils should be able to state one safety rule for fire.

Introduction:
We have learned about keeping our body clean. Today we learn safety at home.
Safety keeps us from getting hurt.

Content:
Sharp objects can cut us.
Examples are knife and scissors.
Fire can burn us badly.
We must not play with fire.
Safe habits keep us safe at home.

Class activity:
Point to sharp objects in the classroom.
Let us practice saying no to fire.

Evaluation questions:
What can sharp objects do?
What should we do if we see fire?
Name one safe habit at home.

Summary:
Sharp objects and fire are dangerous.
We must be careful and follow safety rules.

topics.title: Safety on the road
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate looking left and right.
The pupils should be able to state when to cross the road.

Introduction:
We have learned about safety at home. Today we learn safety on the road.
The road is a dangerous place if we are not careful.

Content:
We must look left and right before crossing.
We use zebra crossing to cross safely.
We must cross with an adult.
Running on the road is not safe.

Class activity:
Let us practice looking left and right.
We will pretend to cross the road together.

Evaluation questions:
What must we do before crossing the road?
Who should we cross with?
Why is running on the road dangerous?

Summary:
We must be careful on the road.
Always look left and right before crossing.

topics.title: The weather around us
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name two types of weather.
The pupils should be able to state what to wear on a sunny day.

Introduction:
We have learned about safety on the road. Today we learn about weather.
The weather changes every day.

Content:
Sunny day means the sun is shining bright.
On sunny days we wear hats and sunglasses.
Rainy day means water falls from the sky.
On rainy days we wear raincoats.

Class activity:
Let us draw a sunny day and a rainy day.
We will make sounds for rain and sun.

Evaluation questions:
What do we wear on a sunny day?
How does the weather feel on a rainy day?
Why do we need to know the weather?

Summary:
Weather changes every day.
We dress differently for different weather.

topics.title: Soil around us
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify sand soil.
The pupils should be able to state where we find soil.

Introduction:
We have learned about weather. Today we learn about soil.
Soil is everywhere around us.

Content:
Sand soil feels rough and dry.
We find sand soil at the beach.
Loam soil feels soft and dark.
We find loam soil in farms.
Soil helps plants grow.

Class activity:
Let us touch different types of soil.
We will feel sand and loam soil.

Evaluation questions:
How does sand soil feel?
Where do we find loam soil?
What does soil help plants do?

Summary:
There are different types of soil.
Soil is important for plants to grow.

topics.title: Plants we can eat
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name two plants we eat.
The pupils should be able to state why plants are good for us.

Introduction:
We have learned about soil. Today we learn about plants we can eat.
Plants give us food to eat.

Content:
Vegetables are plants we eat.
Examples are carrot and spinach.
Fruits are plants we eat.
Examples are banana and orange.
Plants give us vitamins to stay healthy.

Class activity:
Let us taste different fruits and vegetables.
We will name all the plants we can eat.

Evaluation questions:
Name one vegetable you eat.
What fruit did you eat yesterday?
Why are plants good for us?

Summary:
Plants give us food to eat.
They help us stay healthy and strong.

topics.title: Animals and their homes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to match an animal to its home.
The pupils should be able to name two animal homes.

Introduction:
We have learned about plants we can eat. Today we learn about animal homes.
Animals live in different homes.

Content:
A dog lives in a kennel.
A bird lives in a nest.
A fish lives in a pond.
Animals feel safe in their homes.

Class activity:
Let us draw animal homes.
We will match pictures of animals to their homes.

Evaluation questions:
Where does a dog live?
What is a bird's home called?
Why do animals need homes?

Summary:
Animals live in different homes.
Homes keep animals safe and warm.

topics.title: Simple machines at home
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name three simple machines.
The pupils should be able to state the use of a spoon.

Introduction:
We have learned about animal homes. Today we learn about simple machines.
Simple machines help us work easier.

Content:
A spoon helps us eat food.
A scissors helps us cut paper.
A broom helps us sweep the floor.
These are simple machines at home.

Class activity:
Let us use a spoon to pretend to eat.
We will practice cutting with scissors.

Evaluation questions:
What does a spoon help us do?
Name one simple machine at home.
How do machines help us?

Summary:
Simple machines make work easier.
We use them every day at home.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer questions about term work.
The pupils should be able to identify pictures from term topics.

Introduction:
We have learned many things this term. Today we revise and assess.
Let us remember all we learned.

Content:
We learned about keeping our body clean.
We learned about healthy food.
We learned about safety at home and on the road.
We learned about weather and soil.
We learned about plants, animals and simple machines.

Class activity:
Let us play a game to remember what we learned.
We will look at pictures and name them.

Evaluation questions:
What should we do to keep our body clean?
Name one healthy food.
How do we stay safe on the road?
What is soil used for?

Summary:
We learned many important things this term.
Let us remember them to stay healthy and safe.
